memoryText: God said to Moses, I AM WHO I AM. And he said, Say this to the people of Israel: I AM has sent me to you.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Exodus 3:14 slowly, several times, and then try to say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Exodus 3:14 gives you a name to carry with you, and it is not an easy one. “I AM WHO I AM.” It is the most compact statement about God in the Bible, and it has been a source of wonder for the people of God for three thousand years.

Begin with the simplicity of it. God does not say, “I am the powerful one,” or “I am the king,” or “I am the one who will save you.” He says, “I AM.” He is. He exists. He is the source of all that is, and he needs nothing. Before there was anything, there was God.

Notice who God says this to. It is not to philosophers or scholars. It is to a shepherd who is afraid, in the middle of a desert. The God who exists in himself, who does not depend on anything, has come to a nobody in a wilderness to say that he will rescue a nation of slaves. The greatest being in the universe is the one who sees the affliction of his people.

And notice the second half: “I AM has sent me to you.” The name is not just a statement about God’s nature. It is a promise to his people. He will be there. He will be what they need. “I will be with you,” he said to Moses in verse 12, and the name is the guarantee.

For the Christian, there is a final note. Jesus said, “Before Abraham was, I am” (John 8:58). The one who spoke from the bush became flesh and walked among us. Everything that is true of God’s name is true of Jesus.
weekInReview: This week you began the book of Exodus. You read how a new king arose who did not know Joseph, how Israel was enslaved, and how two midwives saved the Hebrew boys. You watched Moses be born, hidden in a basket, raised in Pharaoh’s house, and driven into the wilderness. You stood with him at the burning bush and heard God reveal his name. You saw him offer every excuse and God answer each with himself. On the doctrinal day, you studied the existence and attributes of God, from his self-existence in the name I AM to his character of mercy and justice in Exodus 34. In Psalm 106, you read a confession of Israel’s early failures and heard the line that holds it together: God saved them for his name’s sake. The week taught that God sees, hears, and remembers, and that he comes down to rescue.
reflectionQuestions: Moses had a list of excuses, and God answered each one with a promise of his own presence. What is your list of excuses for something God has asked of you? Write them down, and next to each one write a promise from God.
How does Jesus’ statement, “Before Abraham was, I am,” change the way you read the burning bush? What does it mean to you that the God of Exodus 3 has come in the flesh?
Which part of the description in Exodus 34:6-7 do you find hardest to believe about God? Why? How would your life change if you believed it more fully?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that he sees, hears, and knows.
Rest in who he is, and tell him what you are laying down this Sabbath.
Thank him for Jesus, in whom his name is fulfilled.
